niche: a national statistics office's new private rents measure compiled from the tenancy bond register: the weekly rent payable on every bonded dwelling at quarter ends for the same dwellings a year apart, continuing tenancies' rises seen only through optional bond top-ups and a small rent panel drawn in 2018, re-lettings priced against the tenancy before them across the register's March 2023 migration, the December 2026 quarter projected and the figure bridged to the survey-based series
answer: to be filled from generator/figures.json when the pack is cut
analyst_test: The careful pass conforms the register, links each re-letting to the tenancy before it by property identifier, reads the bond top-ups as the record of every rent rise or carries the old panel's continuing rents to every tenancy, prices each re-letting against the earlier tenancy's starting rent and carries the September figure into December, so it drops the longest tenancies' catch-up, prices the rises small landlords never lodged at nothing or the build-to-rent operators' reviews at the panel's, double counts the earlier tenancy's own rises and misses the quarter that leaves the year, landing the measure, its projection and its bridge outside the golden's ranges in different directions.
domain_test: Every result is a quantity an official statistics office produces when it compiles a price series from an administrative register: a register conformed across a system migration, the completeness of its optional change records measured on a linked survey panel and carried to the register's landlord mix, a matched-dwelling ratio of totals with its sampling interval, a projection from the reviews that fall due, and a bridge to the survey-based figure; swap tenancies for employees and the payroll register records every pay change, there is no optional record to measure, no panel to calibrate it against and nothing left to estimate.
layer1: two register extracts in two schemas: the legacy system to 5 March 2023 (free-text addresses, legacy bond and landlord numbers, rent as an amount with a frequency) and the online system from 6 March 2023 (property identifiers for new lodgements, re-keyed landlord identifiers, weekly rent), with the active bonds migrated keeping their free-text addresses

one tenancy across several records: bond transfers when a property is sold with the tenant in place, changes of tenant parties, re-sent lodgements, refunds that close a bond weeks after the tenancy ends
rents as weekly, fortnightly or monthly amounts, a few keyed in error by a factor of ten, rounded to five or ten dollars
areas recoded to the July 2024 regions through a concordance, three old areas split between two regions
the rent panel's own record: quarterly rents on the fifteenth of the middle month, missed quarters, replacements drawn from the 2017 frame, reported landlord type
a published survey-based series and a release calendar beside unrelated housing series
stakeholder_role: the manager of prices statistics at the national statistics office, preparing the launch of the bond-based private rents measure with the December 2026 quarter

world.geography: Penmarra, a fictional self-governing island state in the South Pacific (New Zealand-style setting and names)

driver: A change in the amount every member of a stock pays is wanted, but the register records a member's amount only when it enters and, by choice, when it rises: small holders' members are recorded for a minority of rises, mostly the large ones, while large holders record every rise; the unrecorded rises are measured on a small panel drawn before the large holders' members existed, so each holder class takes its own rate carried to each area's mix; each unit that changed members is priced against the amount the member before was paying, found across a key change that left the longest-held units without a key; and the next period is projected from when each member's rise falls due.
driver_concrete: Private rents on the bond measure compare total weekly rent payable on bonded dwellings at quarter ends a year apart; small landlords lodge a bond top-up for about a quarter of their rent rises, mostly the large ones, while the build-to-rent operators lodge every one, so continuing tenancies' rises are measured on the Penmarra Statistics Office's 2018 rent panel linked to the register for small landlords and on the operators' complete top-ups for theirs, weighted to each region's mix; each re-letting is priced against the earlier tenancy's paying rent, found by address for the earlier tenancies that predate the March 2023 migration (the longest, with the largest catch-up); and the December 2026 quarter is projected from the anniversaries and portfolio reviews that fall in it.
stump: The careful pass links re-lettings by property identifier, reads the top-ups as every rise and prices re-lettings from the earlier starting rent, filing a September 2026 measure well away from the golden and a December figure carried from September; correcting any one of the three still leaves the measure outside its range, and each correction moves it a different way.
results: R1 bonded tenancies held at 30 September 2026 by region and landlord class on one tenancy record; R2 dwellings re-let in the year to September 2026 and the share whose earlier tenancy is identified; R3 continuing tenancies' rises (share with a rise, average rise) by landlord class; R4 the average rise at re-letting over the earlier tenancy's paying rent; R5 the measure's annual change to September 2026 by region and nationally, with the back series from March 2022; R6 the 90 per cent interval on the national September 2026 figure; R7 the annual change to the December 2026 quarter with its range; R8 the bridge from the survey-based September 2026 figure to the new measure

differentiation.task5: task5 completes an administrative census caught early, report by report, by the cause of each outstanding report; here nothing is late: every bond event is in, and what the register never records (rent rises not lodged) is measured on a linked panel and carried to the register's landlord mix, beside a re-letting linkage across a migration and a projection.
differentiation.task6: task6 weights trace samples by an inherited inclusion probability, fills hours a store dropped and dates incident onsets; here there is no sample weight to recover and no gap in time: the register is complete for what it records, and the work is the completeness of an optional record, the linkage of tenancies across a key change, and a forward projection.
differentiation.task14_v2: architecture 2 grossed a voluntary document list up by its completeness measured where an outside register covers it; here a register's optional change records are corrected by a survey panel linked to it, inside a matched-unit price measure with a projection and a bridge, and the two share no result.
differentiation.mark196: Mark's 196 recovers scam cases neither of two capture channels saw from their overlap, with one channel produced by the unit's own follow-up; here there is no capture-recapture: a register's optional change records are corrected by a linked survey panel inside a matched-dwelling price measure, and the answer is a conformed series with a projection.

lineage.fate: landed: the stage-4 leak reader, reading blind, filed the golden docket with a matched-line ratio shrunk by dollars; judge stump power moderate
lineage.driver: Each unit's amount in the latest period is seen only through its own report, which leaves some items out entirely and understates the amounts of those it keeps, each unit at its own rate; the correction for a kept item's amount is the unit's understatement measured on the items its report kept in the closed periods, not its overall share reported (which carries the items it left out), and that measure is noise on a short record, so it is weighted toward the common rate by the number of items the record holds; the grain alone or the weighting alone each reproduce the last closed period worse than no correction.
lineage.stump: A competent analyst measures each faculty member's completeness as the share of their 2021 to 2025 register remuneration they disclosed, back-tests it on 2025 against the faculty-wide ratio and the disclosures at face value, finds face value closest and sends five faithful disclosers in place of five long-record under-reporters; each person's matched-line ratio unweighted sends thin-record faculty instead, and the overall share weighted by the record sends the faculty who leave small relationships out.

lineage.driver: Each unit's amount in the latest period is seen only through its own report, which covers only what had happened by the day the report was made, while the closed periods' records date every event in the full period; the unit's reporting error must be measured with each earlier report compared against the events up to its own date, and the latest report grossed up for the part of the period it could not yet see, so units that reported early look like under-reporters and units that reported early this time look small to the natural full-period comparison.
lineage.stump: A strong analyst builds each faculty member's matched-line ratio weighted toward the faculty's, compares every disclosure with the register's whole program year, finds it closest to 2025 among the whole-year corrections and sends five faculty whose earlier December disclosures made them look like under-reporters in place of five who submitted their 2026 disclosures in early December, before their retainers' December installments.

lineage.driver: A total is wanted for the part of a population that no outside record covers, and the only evidence is a second list its members supplied voluntarily; the share of that list that was supplied is measured on the part of the population an outside record does cover, over every member and not only those who supplied something, separately for the items each member had and had not already declared, after the outside record's items paid through an intermediary are traced to the intermediary's entry on the list; the supplied items for the uncovered part are then raised by those shares, and the result is checked where declared items can be compared across the two parts.
lineage.stump: The careful pass grosses the uploaded outside forms up by the completeness of the faculty who uploaded something, taking a confirmation that no form was received at its word, pools named and left-off companies in one rate, and counts a manufacturer whose fees an agency paid as a form never uploaded; each of the three moves the estimate of remuneration not shown by a different amount in a different direction, and a run that corrects one still files a figure outside the range.
